body:
`String` isn't `Copy`, so it makes sense that `Copy` is no longer derivable on `Target`.

Removing `Copy` from things can sometimes result in huge ergonomic pains, but based on the fact that your code compiles and I haven't seen a `.clone()` explosion yet, I'm going to guess that it wasn't *that* bad in this case.

I think in this case, it's better to call it the "continuation prompt". That's not naming from our code, it's terminology that's established from the shell. (See e.g. [this answer](https://unix.stackexchange.com/a/193660/379272))
Same here: in almost all shells, if you look at the init scripts, the variable/function that controls this is named some variant of `RIGHT_PROMPT`.
Should this be `profile_name`? Or is `prompt_name` correct in this context?
